newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
MID-AIR PLANE COLLISION NEAR DELHI KILLS 351

A Saudi Airlines Boeing-747 collided in mid-air with a chartered Kazakhistan airliner, killing all 351 people aboard the two planes. Most of the victims were Indian. The collision was over Haryana and about 75 km west of Delhi. The director-general of civil aviation said there was no information about survivors. Sources said so far more than 200 bodies had been recovered from the accident site, where the wreckage of the two planes was strewn over a radius of six km.
The Economic Times
CHRYSLER KEEN ON BANGALORE PLANT

U.S. car major Crysler Corporation is keen to put up a car plant in Bangalore. Crysler's rivals Ford and General Motors (GM) have already set up in India. Official sources said Crysler was ready to invest around 20 billion rupees for the car plant. It has has signed an MoU with the Karnataka government. The market area targeted by Crysler is not known but sources said it could be the 1000 cc segment. Unlike GM, tied up with Hindustan Motors, and Ford, with Mahindra and Mahindra, Crysler could come up with a 100 percent subsidiary of its own, the sources said.
CENTRAL BANK CUTS PRIME LENDING

The Central Bank of India has slashed its prime lending rate (PLR) to 15 percent from 16.5 percent. The bank announced a maximum spread of four percent over the PLR. In line with the monetary policy for the second half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), interest rates on post shipment rupee export credit beyond 90 days and up to six months from the date of shipment was also lowered to 16 percent.
DEFER DIVESTMENT UNTIL, ONGC SAYS

The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) expressed its reluctance over government plans for possible disinvestment in mid-1997. Company sources said ONGC had asked the petroleum ministry to defer the government's disinvestment plans till 1998. Recently, the core group of secretaries had referred 40 public sector units, including ONGC, to the disinvestment commission for disinvestment in the third tranche. Instead, the oil major asked the government to come out with a clear policy on pricing of crude. This was required immediately because the prospective investors would be keen to know about the future profitability of the company before making any investment decision, sources added.
Financial Express
BAT PROPOSES 11 BLN RUPEE INVESTMENT

BAT is believed to have approached the government with a proposal to invest up to 11 billion rupees in a wholly-owned investment subsidiary in India. The proposed holding company would serve as an investment company for future projects of the international tobacco and insurance giant, including new joint ventures. BAT is expected to formally apply to the Foreign Investment Promotion Board after the impasse over ITC was sorted out.
MAJOR RELIEF FOR SPINNING, GRANITE, FLORICULMRE EOUS

The government has given some major relief to 1OO percent export-oriented spinning, as well as horticulture/floriculture and granite units, to give them an edge in the global market. Cotton spinning units have been permitted to export yarn, in hank form, in the count groups 1-60, without restriction. The import basket for horticulture/floriculture units was enlarged to include five more items. The government also rationalised wastage norms for granite export oriented units.
PANEL CHARTS STRATEGY TO CHECK FUNDS DIVERSION

The Planning Commission is working on a strategy to check the diversion of plan funds for non-plan activities by state governments. Sources in the commission said as part of the Ninth Plan exercise, a clearer division between plan and non-plan expenditure was being worked out. This would check diversion of funds for non-plan activities and help in chanelling funds earmarked for intended purposes. Some weaker states, sources said, were notorious for diverting plan funds for non-plan activities which did not serve developmental needs.
FIAT SETS PACE FOR LOCALISATION OF UNO

A host of component suppliers for Italian automaker Fiat have forged alliances with Indian counterparts for the Uno project. The car is being assembled in technical collaboration with Premier Automobiles at the company's Kurla plant in Bombay. Fiat is keen on increasing the pace of localisation of components for the Uno. It is targeting a level of 80 percent by the end of 1997. Fiat's desire to pick a stake in the Uno project is being evaluated. The two parties have already announced plans to set up a separate greenfield facility to produce the Palio near Pune, in which Fiat will have a majority holding.
PASSBOOK SCHEME HIT BY NEW CONDITIONS

The passbook scheme for select categories of exporters has been hit by new conditions set by the customs authorities. The scheme was conceived as an improvement over the advance licence plan in the current export-import policy. Exporters benefiting from the scheme included export, trading and star trading houses, along with manufacturer-exporters. Customs authorities refused to enter the customs duty credit in the passbooks issued to exporters on the input-output norms because they contained provisions for wastage in the process of manufacture of items for export.
ASSOCHAM BLUEPRINT ON REFORMS

The Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry has prepared a blueprint on reforms in response to the prime minister's call for concrete suggestions on economic revival. The plan has suggestions on boosting industrial growth, exports, state of the capital market, high interest rates and infrastructure bottlenecks. It called for delinking economic issues from politics so that economic decisions were not guided by short-term political considerations. It said India should create a long-term debt market where corporates could raise funds at around average costs of capital charged by financial institutions.
CDC, LUCKY GOLDSTAR TO HAVE STAKE IN NINL

The Commonwealth Development Corporation (CDC) of Britain and Lucky Goldstar of South Korea will have equity participation in Neelachal Ispat Nigam's (NINL) proposed 15 billion rupee integrated steel project in Orissa. While CDC offered to contribute between 700 million and one billion rupees, Goldstar proposed an investment of up to one billion rupees. NINL may offer a stake of about 20 percent to the two firms. Division of the equity between the two companies has yet to be decided.
Business Standard
OECF REFUSES TO FUND KOEL KARO PROJECT

The Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund (OECF) of Japan turned down the government's request for funding the 24 billion rupee, 710 mw Koel Karo hydel project in Bihar. OECF refused to provide funds on the ground that the two billion rupee rehabilitation cost of the project was on the higher side. Moreover, it was pointed out there had been a prolonged protest against the project by local residents for the past 10 to 15 years. The government approached OECF after being pressured by Bihar chief minister Laloo Yadav who wanted the project, languishing from 1980, to be implemented soon.
The Observer
BASIC TELECOM OPERATORS UNABLE TO PAY LICENCE FEE

Two weeks have passed since the ultimatum was set on letter of intent holders of basic telecommunication service by the communication ministry. But companies have failed to pay the licence fee. This was due to the banks' refusal to finance the basic service projects until the issues relating to the licence and interconnect pact are resolved. The private sector companies have not received any reply from the department of telecommunications regarding the issues raised by them. This has affected the cellular operators as well. The banks have refused to finance their operations. The cellular operators, who were to start operations by November/December, are yet to be alloted frequencies for operation.
PETROLEUM SECTOR NEEDS 2000 BLN RUPEES

The petroleum sector requires a 2000 billion rupee investment in the Ninth Plan period (1997/2002). 75 percent of this was expected to be met through domestic and foreign capital, beside assistance from external multilateral agencies, petroleum ministry estimates reveal. Refining would need around 700 billion rupees, the ministry projected. Marketing and distribution, exploration and production would require investments of 500 billion rupees and 800 billion rupees, respectively, ministry officials said. The ministry expected 50 percent of the amount from the private sector, indigenous industry and oil multinationals.
